products.title: Five Quiet Forces That Shape Your Life
products.shortDescription: Five ideas that have been running your life without your permission — and one specific thing to do about each.
products.longDescription: Five concepts compressed into a single sitting. The Spotlight Effect, Identity-Based Habits, the Sunk Cost Fallacy, the Fundamental Attribution Error, and the practice of looking foolish on purpose — each with one exercise to try this week.

products.title: The Quiet Forces
products.tagline: Seven forces shaping how you move through your own life.
products.shortDescription: The opening volume — the foundational forces that shape how you see yourself, and the small moves that begin to change them.
products.longDescription: Seven psychological forces quietly running the way you live with yourself — from the Butterfly Effect that magnifies the smallest moves, to the Pareto Principle that hides where the real work is. Each force gets its origin story, its research, its examples, and a counter-move you can try this week.

forces.name: The Butterfly Effect
forces.tagline: Why the smallest moves are usually the ones doing the real work.

forces.name: Crab Mentality
forces.tagline: The oldest form of sabotage — and the one most likely to come from people who love you.

forces.name: The Spotlight Effect
forces.tagline: The exhausting illusion that everyone is looking at you.

forces.name: The Arrival Fallacy
forces.tagline: The quiet disappointment of getting what you wanted.

forces.name: Identity-Based Habits
forces.tagline: Why changing who you believe you are changes everything downstream.

forces.name: The Lindy Effect
forces.tagline: Why the oldest ideas are usually the most trustworthy.

forces.name: The Pareto Principle
forces.tagline: Most of your life is being produced by a small fraction of your life.

products.pullQuote: You cannot fight what you cannot name. But once you name it, it begins to lose.

products.title: The Quiet Forces
products.tagline: Five cognitive biases distorting your judgment.
products.shortDescription: The next set of forces — the ones quietly shaping the way you decide what's worth chasing and what's worth quitting.
products.longDescription: Five cognitive biases that quietly hijack your thinking, from the Dunning-Kruger overconfidence trap to the Sunk Cost Fallacy that keeps you in the wrong room. Each chapter is a short field guide to one bias and the specific moves that loosen its grip.

forces.name: The Dunning-Kruger Effect
forces.tagline: Why the people who know least are the most certain.

forces.name: Parkinson's Law
forces.tagline: Why the work always expands to fill the time you give it.

forces.name: Loss Aversion
forces.tagline: Why losing $100 hurts more than gaining $100 helps.

forces.name: Survivorship Bias
forces.tagline: Why the lessons of the winners are usually the wrong lessons.

forces.name: The Sunk Cost Fallacy
forces.tagline: Why the cost of staying is hidden in plain sight.

products.metaDescription: Volume II of The Quiet Forces — a 67-page workbook on five cognitive biases distorting your judgment.

products.title: The Quiet Forces
products.tagline: Five social forces shaping how you see other people.
products.shortDescription: The closing volume of the trilogy — the forces that govern how you read other people, and how they read you.
products.longDescription: Five social forces that decide who you trust, what you copy, and what you mistake for character. From the Fundamental Attribution Error to the Halo Effect, each chapter explains the force, the research behind it, and a specific way to push back this week.

forces.name: The Fundamental Attribution Error
forces.tagline: Why their behavior is character and yours is circumstance.

forces.name: Social Proof
forces.tagline: Why the crowd is the most persuasive argument no one has made.

forces.name: The Overton Window
forces.tagline: Why what feels normal today was unthinkable a decade ago.

forces.name: Reciprocity
forces.tagline: Why the smallest gift creates the largest obligation.

forces.name: The Halo Effect
forces.tagline: Why one good trait persuades you of every other good trait.

products.metaDescription: Volume III of The Quiet Forces — a 68-page workbook on five social forces shaping how you see other people.

products.title: The Quiet Work
products.tagline: A twelve-week guided practice. The companion to the trilogy.
products.shortDescription: Eighty-four daily prompts across four phases — The Mirror, The Edit, The Build, The Integration — that turn the ideas into a real change in your week.
products.longDescription: A twelve-week guided practice workbook designed as the companion to the trilogy. Four phases — The Mirror, The Edit, The Build, The Integration — broken into eighty-four daily prompts with write-in space. The book the trilogy was always pointing at.

forces.name: The Mirror
forces.tagline: Three weeks of seeing yourself as you actually are.

forces.name: The Edit
forces.tagline: Three weeks of subtracting what isn't yours.

forces.name: The Build
forces.tagline: Three weeks of adding what is.

forces.name: The Integration
forces.tagline: Three weeks of making the change unconscious.
